nodes.line: I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. I start at two in the afternoon and for a month the Carlingford back lane has had somebody in it who is not waiting for bread. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.

Two people have already said no. A light on that lane costs Carlingford $78 and the landlord has said no twice, so we are doing it ourselves. I have rung the number on the letter four times. I'll see you right for it.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

choices.text: two in the afternoon at Carlingford — that's done.
The Lane Light, Carlingford — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Ah. Someone with two working legs.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. The flour for Carlingford comes off a truck at two in the afternoon and last a wet Monday the truck came and the flour did not. Half the street knows and half the street is pretending not to. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

You are the first person to stop all morning. The Carlingford loading zone has had a car in it at two in the afternoon every morning this week and the driver waits in it, which makes it worse. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. Just do not come back empty-handed.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

choices.text: The Loading Zone, Carlingford — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Tomasz, front of house at Carlingford

nodes.line: You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

Not being dramatic about this. Somebody two doors down from Carlingford put up a sign on a wet Monday that says the same six words as ours, in the same order. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. I will know if you skipped a bit.

I am told you do odd jobs. This business was at Telopea before it was at Carlingford, and there is a woman there who still has the original book. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
I had a feeling. Go on.

choices.text: The Sourdough Sign, Carlingford — that's done.
The Old Site, Carlingford — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. Council has been saying the Macarthur pool is at end of life since every second Friday and the crack they keep pointing at is not in the shell. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.

Two people have already said no. We are running a stall for Macarthur on every second Friday and a stall needs $89 of gear that nobody has volunteered to pay for. I have rung the number on the letter four times. I'll see you right for it.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: The Petition Stall, Macarthur — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
Do not mind the mess. It is structural now.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. I coach 70 kids at Macarthur at the second express and three of them have stopped coming without anybody ringing me. Half the street knows and half the street is pretending not to. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

You are the first person to stop all morning. A group has been coming over the Macarthur fence after close and swimming in the dark, which is how Macarthur loses its pool. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. Just do not come back empty-handed.
Go on then. What did you find.

choices.text: The Deep End, Macarthur — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
If you are selling something the answer is no.

Not being dramatic about this. The kiosk at Macarthur has two hundred metres of orange netting in it and a freezer that has been running warm since every second Friday. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. I will know if you skipped a bit.

I am told you do odd jobs. They want everyone from Macarthur to drive to the new centre at Campbelltown, so somebody should go and see whether it is any good. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: The Kiosk Freezer, Macarthur — that's done.
The Aquatic Centre, Macarthur — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
Cash only and no, I am joking. What do you want.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. The rank outside Carramar used to hold nine cars and since the long weekend it holds four, and nobody will say who moved the line. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.

Two people have already said no. Since the rank at Carramar shrank I am $107 a week down, and the association wants that number from somebody who can prove it. I have rung the number on the letter four times. I'll see you right for it.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.
Right you are. Mind the step.
You have got a face like you can keep your mouth shut.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Cars that have never sat in the Carramar queue turn up at twenty past four and take the front of it, and the drivers who waited say nothing. Half the street knows and half the street is pretending not to. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

You are the first person to stop all morning. When the last train into Carramar is late, 21 people come out at once and I have to have cars there before they do. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. Just do not come back empty-handed.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

choices.text: The Late Train, Carramar — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
Right. Talk while I do this.

Not being dramatic about this. I have stood on this door near Carramar for 21 years and since the long weekend somebody has been sending my guests to a different rank. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. I will know if you skipped a bit.

I am told you do odd jobs. The plates working the Carramar rank are dispatched from a depot at Villawood, and the man who runs it has never met a driver he liked. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
Well? I can read your face from here.
Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
